books.title: The Night Train
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Nina was going to visit her grandparents, and the train left at night. She had never slept on a train before.
The train was long and silver, with warm lights in every window. Nina found her little bed and pulled the curtain closed.
'Chug, chug, chug,' sang the wheels as the train rolled through the dark countryside.
Nina peeked out of the window. She saw sleepy villages, dark forests, and the moon following the train.
In the morning the sun came up, and the train stopped at a small station. Her grandparents were waiting on the platform.
Nina hugged them tight. The night train had been the most exciting journey of her life.

books.title: The Clever Rabbit
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Ruby the rabbit lived in a burrow under a big oak tree. She was the cleverest rabbit in the meadow.
One summer the meadow was very dry, and the rabbits could not find enough food. Everyone was worried.
Ruby remembered a garden on the other side of the hill. 'Follow me,' she said to the other rabbits.
She led them through a gap in the fence to a garden full of carrots and lettuce. There was food for everyone.
The rabbits ate their fill and carried some home for the little ones. They thanked Ruby again and again.
From then on, whenever there was a problem, the rabbits asked Ruby first, because clever friends are the best kind.

books.title: The Singing Whale
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Deep in the ocean lived a young whale called Willa. Willa loved to sing, but her songs were quiet and shy.
The other whales sang loud, beautiful songs that travelled for miles. Willa wished she could sing like them.
One day a little lost dolphin heard Willa's soft song and followed it home. 'Your song saved me,' said the dolphin.
Willa realised her quiet song was special. It was gentle, and it helped animals who were lost or afraid.
Soon whales from all over the ocean came to hear Willa sing. Her soft voice made everyone feel calm and safe.
Willa still sings every evening, and now she sings proudly, because the kindest songs are often the quietest ones.

books.title: The Friendly Ghost
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: In an old house on the hill lived a friendly ghost named Boo. He was not scary at all. He just wanted a friend.
One evening, a new family moved into the house. Boo was so excited that he knocked over a vase, and the little boy, Max, heard the noise.
"Who is there?" Max called out. Boo floated down slowly and said, "It is only me, Boo. I am a friendly ghost."
Max was not scared. He showed Boo his toys, and Boo showed Max how to float through the ceiling. They laughed all night long.
From then on, Boo was part of the family. Every evening, Max and Boo played together, and the old house was full of laughter again.
